brief:
Design an extraordinary contemporary Caribbean waterfront estate in Saint Lucia with an estimated property value of US$25 million, approximately six generous bedroom suites, expansive living and entertainment spaces, a memorable entrance, exceptional indoor-outdoor connections, substantial shaded terraces and a rectangular swimming pool.

Aim for sophisticated luxury architecture: a clear architectural idea, hierarchy of primary and subordinate volumes, beautiful proportions, privacy, climatic shading, considered facade depth, coordinated materials and compelling arrival and waterfront elevations. Resolve individual suite allocations, social and service accommodation and actual connected circulation rather than relying on room-capacity labels.

You have creative freedom over composition, spatial organization, number of levels, entrance relationships, roof forms and building arrangement within the canonical compiler's documented capabilities. No three-pavilion arrangement, fixed roof style or predefined mansion template is required. Select your own architectural decisions; the deterministic compiler calculates supported geometry, shared boundaries, openings, floors and stairs.

This experiment requests the supported editable architectural envelope, not complete fit-out, landscaping, terrain or marine engineering. Use the documented flat-site representation; ocean context is conceptual. Lawn/bed surfaces are sufficient landscape reserves; planting and grading are outside this test. A rectangular pool is requested, not an unsupported infinity-edge amenity. Do not claim those unsupported features are constructed.

Use the extended canonical contract faithfully. If your intended architectural decision is unsupported, preserve and disclose that decision or return decision-required; never silently replace it with ordinary rectangles. Do not omit programme or flatten ambitious design merely to claim completion. The resulting architecture will be judged in aerial, arrival, garden and poolside views, separately from schema acceptance and construction fidelity.

requirements.note: Programme counts are read from authored uses; the brief governs.

currentPlan.thesis: A terraced Caribbean courtyard estate recast as a landward arrival bar and elevated guest belvedere framing a long, shaded waterward social sequence. The composition distinguishes a tall ivory arrival/gallery spine, limestone private wings with individually resolved suites, and low bronze-roofed service and outdoor entertaining elements. A compact upper guest-and-owner belvedere gives the arrival elevation and waterfront silhouette sectional hierarchy without turning the estate into a repetitive pavilion field. The south-facing pool terrace remains the primary waterfront room; screens and recessed openings provide selective shade and privacy rather than glazing every facade.

decisions.title: Pitched roof on east-suite-3
decisions.relationship: A pitched roof (hip) stays inside its own room and builds fascia only on edges no other room shares, so abutting a neighbour of any height is valid. It is rejected only where a space is stacked over part of it (lean-to or valley), where an overhang reaches a neighbour, or where rooms overlap.
decisions.softwareRole: Derives, from adjacency alone, which edges of a pitched roof are exposed (fascia only there) and which neighbours it meets; builds the exposed remainder of a partly covered flat roof itself.
decisions.youDecide: Which rooms get a pitched or overhanging roof (a design choice), a flat roof for any space with a room stacked over part of it, and the arrangement when rooms overlap.

findings.compilerNote: The compiler is fail-fast: later construction stages (junction splitting, stair fit, staggered walls, scene support checks) only run after earlier stages pass, so a clean diagnosis is not proof of acceptance.
compilerFirstRejection: media-lounge/east-suite-1: occupied volumes overlap (3.60m vertical). same-level footprints intersect: media-lounge spans x 14..22, z -18..-12 m, east-suite-1 spans x 13..22, z -18..-12 m; they share x 14..22, z -18..-12 m. Revise outlines or placement.

signals.evidence: 12 of 30 interior rooms are identical cells in groups of three or more (6× 9×6 m; 6× 4×6 m).
30 interior rooms share one level; envelope tops span only 4.8 m (6 distinct heights); roof forms: flat, gable, hip.
2 level(s) for 30 interior rooms. A single level is not a defect on its own; this only contributes when combined with other signals.

15 of 30 interior rooms (31% of interior area) have no window: arrival-cloakroom, stair-hall, kitchen, pantry, laundry, service-store, east-private-hall, west-private-hall, east-bath-1, east-bath-2, east-bath-3, west-bath-1, west-bath-2, west-bath-3, upper-landing.
Allocated cells fill 73% of their 55×50 m bounding rectangle: an articulated footprint.
No obvious programme gaps among authored uses.

disposition.note: Some architectural weakness is present but the concept is not judged fundamentally ordinary; physical relationships should be corrected while preserving coherent decisions, and the weaknesses reconsidered where cheap.
